text.p: These were the main headlines from Lithuania's M-1 plus radio station's news report on Tuesday at noon. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- In parliament's plenary session, the legislature passed a law on the prevention of organised crime and also plans to pass the law on property restitution, which was returned by President Algirdas Brazauskas for amendments last month.
- The development of democracy in Lithuania was evaluated as positive at the Council of Europe Parliamentary Assembly.

Lithuanian parliamentarian Bronislovas Kuzmickas said that the Council of Europe monitoring committee was interested in human rights in Lithuania, the law on preventative arrest and the scrapping of the death penalty.

- Two Lithuanian citizens were arrested in the U.S. by Miami police under suspicion that they were trying to sell nuclear weapons and anti-aircraft rockets. The suspects are 36-year-old Alexander Darichev and 29-year-old Alexander Progrebeshski.
